title: Sheafified presentation of modules of differentials
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and let $\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be a morphism of presheaves of commutative rings. The module of differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] $\Omega_{\mathcal B^\#/\mathcal A^\#}$ of the sheafified ring map is canonically the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of the presheaf $U\mapsto\Omega_{\mathcal B(U)/\mathcal A(U)}$, and the identification carries the sectionwise universal derivations to the sheaf universal derivation. Equivalently, both are the cokernel of the sheafified free-module relation map encoding additivity, Leibniz, and annihilation of $\mathcal A$ in the category of sheaf modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Here a derivation of sheaves is a morphism of underlying sheaves of sets satisfying additivity, the Leibniz rule, and vanishing on the image of the base ring on every object; the sheaf module of differentials means the representing module for this derivation functor, with its universal derivation.

source.place: Tag 08TP, lemma-differentials-sheafify and proof (the displayed free-module relation map and exactness of sheafification)

proof.text: Write $\varphi:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$. For a presheaf of sets $T$, put $\mathcal B[T](U)=\bigoplus_{t\in T(U)}\mathcal B(U)[t]$, with restrictions sending $b[t]$ to $b|_V[t|_V]$; this is the free module in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Form $F=\mathcal B[\mathcal B]$ and $E=\mathcal B[\mathcal B\times\mathcal B]\oplus\mathcal B[\mathcal B\times\mathcal B]\oplus\mathcal B[\mathcal A]$. Define $r:E\to F$ by $[(a,b)]\mapsto[a+b]-[a]-[b]$ on the first summand, $[(f,g)]\mapsto[fg]-g[f]-f[g]$ on the second, and $[h]\mapsto[\varphi(h)]$ on the third. Restrictions commute with these formulas because they preserve addition, multiplication and $\varphi$. The sectionwise quotient $P(U)=F(U)/\operatorname{im}r_U$ is $\Omega_{\mathcal B(U)/\mathcal A(U)}$ with $d_U(b)$ the class of $[b]$, by the explicit quotient construction in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Thus $P$ is the desired presheaf of differentials, with restrictions $d_U(b)\mapsto d_V(b|_V)$.

source.place: Tag 08TP, lemma-differentials-sheafify, displayed presheaf map; Algebra Tags 07BK and 00RO

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface] with the presheaf ring $\mathcal O=\mathcal B$ to $E,F,P$. Their abelian sheafifications acquire the canonical $\mathcal B^\#$-module structures and $r$ and $F\to P$ sheafify to linear maps. By [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact], the abelian cokernel presentation $E\xrightarrow r F\to P\to0$ sheafifies to a cokernel presentation. The cokernel in $\mathcal B^\#$-module sheaves has the same underlying abelian cokernel by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Consequently $Q=P^\#$, with $q:F^\#\to Q$, is the cokernel of $r^\#:E^\#\to F^\#$ in module sheaves.

source.place: Tag 08TP, last sentence; Tag 03CY, lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules; Tag 03EI, lemma-sheafification-exact

proof.text: By [lem-pc-sites-sheafification-underlying-sets], the underlying set maps $\mathcal A\to\mathcal A^\#$ and $\mathcal B\to\mathcal B^\#$ are set sheafifications. The map $\mathcal B\times\mathcal B\to\mathcal B^\#\times\mathcal B^\#$ is also a set sheafification: by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local], a pair of sheafified sections lifts locally to two original sections after taking a common covering refinement, and two lifts of the pair agree after a further common refinement. Given a map from $\mathcal B\times\mathcal B$ into any sheaf of sets, apply it to these local lifts; local equality makes their values agree on overlaps, so they glue uniquely. This is exactly the universal property of sheafification. The common refinements are obtained by the covering pullback and composition axioms in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology].

source.place: Tag 08TP, identification of the sheafified free terms; Sites Tags 00YR and 00WK

proof.text: For each $T=\mathcal B,\mathcal B\times\mathcal B,\mathcal A$ and any sheaf $N$ of $\mathcal B^\#$-modules, [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface] gives $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal B^\#}(\mathcal B[T]^\#,N)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal B}(\mathcal B[T],N)$. A map on the right is uniquely the linear extension of a map of set presheaves $T\to|N|$: send $\sum b_t[t]$ to $\sum b_t v(t)$. Conversely evaluating at $[t]$ recovers $v$, and both constructions commute with restrictions. By the universal property [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] and Step 3 this equals $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C)}(T^\#,|N|)$. Thus $\mathcal B[T]^\#$ is the free $\mathcal B^\#$-module sheaf on $T^\#$, with its specified generators. In particular $F^\#$ is free on $\mathcal B^\#$.

source.place: Tag 08TP, sentence identifying the sheaves in the presentation; Tag 04BL, lemma-universal-module, free-module notation

proof.text: The same adjunction identifies $E^\#$ with the sum of the two free sheaves on $\mathcal B^\#\times\mathcal B^\#$ and the free sheaf on $\mathcal A^\#$: a map from $E^\#$ to $N$ is just three maps from its summands, by [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface]. Under these identifications $r^\#$ is the sheaf relation map with the three formulas of Step 1, now for sheafified sections. Indeed both maps take the original generators to those displayed relations; equality on the original generators implies equality before sheafification by linear extension and then after sheafification by uniqueness in that adjunction. This also proves that sheafifying introduces no additional choice in the relation map.

source.place: Tag 08TP, sheafified presentation compared with equation-define-module-differentials

proof.text: Let $j:\mathcal B^\#\to|F^\#|$ be the free-generator map from Step 4 and put $d=qj$. The three relations of Step 5 vanish in $Q$, so $d(a+b)=d(a)+d(b)$, $d(fg)=g\,d(f)+f\,d(g)$ and $d(\varphi^\#(h))=0$ for sections of the sheafified rings. Thus $d$ is a sheaf $\mathcal A^\#$-derivation. For any $\mathcal B^\#$-module sheaf $N$ and any such derivation $D:\mathcal B^\#\to N$, Step 4 extends $D$ uniquely to a linear map $v:F^\#\to N$. Each of the three generator formulas for $vr^\#$ is zero by the corresponding derivation identity, hence $vr^\#=0$. The cokernel property of Step 2 gives a unique $\alpha:Q\to N$ with $\alpha q=v$, and therefore $\alpha d=D$. Conversely a linear map $\alpha$ produces the derivation $\alpha d$. These constructions are inverse: $\alpha q$ is determined by its generator values and a map out of the cokernel is determined after $q$. This verifies the representing property for sheaf derivations directly.

source.place: Tag 04BL, lemma-universal-module, proof after equation-define-module-differentials; Tag 04BN, definition-module-differentials

proof.text: It follows that $(Q,d)$ is a module of differentials of $\mathcal A^\#\to\mathcal B^\#$. If $(\Omega,d_{\mathrm{sh}})$ is any other representing module, apply the two universal properties to obtain maps $Q\to\Omega$ and $\Omega\to Q$ carrying the universal derivations to each other. Each composite fixes the universal derivation and hence is the identity by uniqueness. This gives the canonical isomorphism $P^\#=Q\cong\Omega_{\mathcal B^\#/\mathcal A^\#}$. For $b\in\mathcal B(U)$, the image of $d_U(b)$ in $Q(U)$ is $q([\eta_{\mathcal B}(b)])=d(\eta_{\mathcal B}(b))$, so the isomorphism carries every sectionwise universal derivation to $d_{\mathrm{sh}}$. Steps 2 and 5 give exactly the asserted common sheafified-cokernel presentation, completing all clauses.

lean.note: The sheaf differential module is expressed by its representing property among sheaf modules, using Mathlib Derivation' on the underlying presheaf. The unique isomorphism is normalized on the universal derivation and original sectionwise differentials. Helpers specialize existing free-module and sheafification functors; no alternative differential-module construction is introduced. The three free summands are encoded as the free module on their disjoint union.
